scope: 02_rules.md:Answered question OQ-17 — Dependency vulnerability and update policy

topics.topic: HTTP status and body for malformed snapshot-publication requests
questions: What HTTP answer must request decoding return for a malformed snapshot publication?
What exact HTTP status and body must request decoding return for a malformed snapshot-publication body?
What HTTP status and body must request decoding return for a snapshot publication with a missing or wrongly typed field?

quotes:
A body that lacks a required field or carries one of the wrong type is
refused by request decoding before the bearer credential is checked: it is
not an import attempt, gets no `import_id` and writes no record.
judgement.why: The HTTP status and response-body representation of request-decoding failures are State 6 API-contract details.

topics.topic: Rule or evidence determining vulnerability applicability for deployment blocking
questions: What makes a known vulnerability count as affecting the portal for the deploy decision, and who or what decides that applicability?
What evidence or rule determines that a known vulnerability ‘affects the portal’ and therefore blocks deployment?
What evidence or rule determines that a known vulnerability affects the portal and therefore blocks deployment?

quotes:
Before a deploy, the pinned versions are checked against a public
   known-vulnerability database; a pin with a known vulnerability that affects
   the portal is not deployed until it is updated through the Factory route.
   A check that cannot complete does not pass, and the deploy waits. How the
   check is run (its tool, its database, the resolved set it covers) is a
   deployment procedure, not a portal rule, carried to the deploy route.
No deploy ships a pin with a known vulnerability affecting the portal.
The pre-deploy vulnerability check of those pins passes.
judgement.divergence: One deployment gate blocks every advisory affecting a shipped package, while another permits an advisory after judging its vulnerable feature unreachable; the deployment operator and release users notice whether the release proceeds.
judgement.why: The blocking rule depends on whether a vulnerability affects the portal but supplies no applicability criterion or decision authority.

witness.initial: A pinned library in the proposed deployment has a published advisory limited to an optional feature the portal does not use.
events: The pre-deploy vulnerability check reports the advisory.
The deployment operator applies A32 to decide whether the release may proceed.
outcomes: The release is blocked because every advisory for a shipped pinned library is treated as affecting the portal.
The release proceeds because the optional vulnerable feature is judged unreachable by the portal.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users receiving or not receiving the release.
basis:
Before a deploy, the pinned versions are checked against a public
   known-vulnerability database; a pin with a known vulnerability that affects
   the portal is not deployed until it is updated through the Factory route.
   A check that cannot complete does not pass, and the deploy waits. How the
   check is run (its tool, its database, the resolved set it covers) is a
   deployment procedure, not a portal rule, carried to the deploy route.

questions: After hashing parameters change, does a successful authentication replace an older valid password hash with a hash using the current parameters?
After hashing parameters change through the Factory route, must a successful login rehash an existing password hash that uses the previous parameters?

quotes:
Writes one `StaffSession` and one `AuditRecord` per success; one
`AuditRecord` per rejection.
judgement.why: The later authentication operation exhaustively states that a successful login writes only a StaffSession and AuditRecord, so it does not replace the password hash.

topics.topic: Precision, rounding, and quantization of overall-progress quotients
questions: When the overall-progress quotient has more than two fractional digits, what precision and rounding rule determine the returned Decimal?
At what precision and with what final quantization must a non-terminating overall-progress quotient be returned?

quotes:
`Decimal`, 2 fraction digits, `ROUND_HALF_UP` at derivation boundaries;
  stored amounts are already 2-digit exact.
judgement.why: The general derivation-boundary rule requires the derived overall-progress Decimal to be quantized half-up to two fraction digits.

topics.topic: ProjectOverview shape and outcome when Registry context retrieval fails after validation
questions: What is the exact ProjectOverview shape and validation rule when post-guard Registry context retrieval fails?
What is the exact ProjectOverview shape and outcome when validation succeeds but the subsequent Registry context read fails?

judgement.why: This is the same ProjectOverview availability question on unchanged texts already decided by P17.

precedent.topic: ProjectOverview schema and conditional project availability after Registry context-read failure
quotes:
`ProjectOverview`: six pairs — project, budget, expenses, progress, payments,
photos — each a `ViewAvailability` and a value present only when available.

A21 (derived at read time, nothing persisted), A27 and Factory
`d2c4511ea119`: a part whose builder answers `ScopedNotFoundError` is
`not_configured`, a persistence or Registry failure `temporarily_unavailable`;
no zero is fabricated; viewer photos are client-visible only.
precedent.why: State 5 defines ProjectOverview as six availability/value pairs and converts a Registry context failure into temporary unavailability.

topics.topic: Label and displayed value when completed work equals total payments
questions: Which label and displayed value apply when completed work value exactly equals payments total?

quotes:
Work balance: `completed work value − payments total`; sign selects the
  presentation label (`Completed ahead of payments` / absolute value as
  `Unused advance payment`).

`PaymentSummaryView` fields: `payments: list[PaymentView]`,
  `payments_total: Decimal`, `completed_work_total: Decimal`,
  `work_balance: Decimal`, `balance_label: WorkBalanceLabel`.
judgement.divergence: At a zero balance, one implementation returns `balanced` while another assigns zero to `completed_ahead_of_payments` or `unused_advance_payment`; the viewer and API client observe the different label.
judgement.why: The texts define a `balanced` label and say the sign selects a label but never map the zero sign to that label.

witness.initial: A project has completed work value EUR 100.00 and payments total EUR 100.00.
events: An authenticated viewer opens the project and reads its payments and work balance.
outcomes: The payment summary returns `work_balance` 0.00 and assigns one of the two labels named in A9.
witness.observer: The viewer and any API client consuming the payment summary.
basis:
An authenticated viewer sees the list of their assigned projects, opens one,
and reads: Registry project context, budget summary with source and ordered
sections, included and excluded confirmed expenses with `Other expenses`
separate, client-visible documents, work progress and completed work value,
payments and work balance, and the chronological photo gallery.

For an active project an operator can: correct, include, or exclude an
expense; allocate or manually split it across sections or `Other expenses`
(allocation sum equals the expense total; automatic proportional split is
forbidden); update manual work progress per section (0–100%); register work
payments (idempotent by stable payment identity); publish progress photos and
manage caption, section association, and visibility; maintain the manual
budget; review and activate imported budget versions.

Work balance: `completed work value − payments total`; sign selects the
  presentation label (`Completed ahead of payments` / absolute value as
  `Unused advance payment`).
